title: Diagnostic value of ultrasound elastography in differentiating malignant and benign lesions of the breast with combined use of real time shear wave elastography and compression elastography compared to MRI.
summary:
The aim of the study is to improve diagnostic accuracy with regard to the differentiation of benign and malignant findings in the breast and thus to optimize early detection and follow-up. Routine breast cancer screening is currently performed by mammography and follow-up by mammography and ultrasound examination.
The study-related examination consists of an imaging technique approved for breast diagnosis - elastography. Ultrasound elastography is a medical imaging procedure performed using an ultrasound machine. Unlike mammography, the procedure works entirely without ionizing radiation (X-rays). Instead, all measurements are made using ultrasound waves emitted by the device, which are reflected by the tissue and converted into image data.
Ultrasound elastography can be divided into two different procedures: shear wave elastography and compression elastography. With the help of ultrasound waves and light to moderate pressure, which the examiner exerts with the transducer on the tissue to be examined, the ultrasound device can measure the tissue deformation. The tissue hardness is then compared to that of normal mammary gland tissue. According to current research, the use of sonography and elastography poses no health risks.
This study examination of approximately 20 minutes is performed as part of a regular appointment; there is no separate appointment as part of the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient capable of giving consent.
- MR mammography performed with histologically confirmed findings, planned biopsy or clearly benign findings in mammography and sonography that can be clearly assigned to an entity.
- MR examination maximum 4 weeks ago.
- Patient has a regular appointment for MR examination or other scheduled examination in the Radiology Department of the University Women's Hospital.
- Age ≥18 years.
- Written informed consent from the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnant or breastfeeding patients.
- Significantly restricted examination conditions (lying on the back is not possible, limited abduction or elevation of the arm).
